activities.title: Construct a thesaurus entry for University Libraries
activities.instructions_md: 1. Construct a thesaurus entry for the term University Libraries, including one Broader Term, two Narrower Terms, two Related Terms, and one UF reference.

activities.title: Construct a thesaurus entry for Information Literacy
activities.instructions_md: 2. Construct a thesaurus entry for the term Information Literacy, and justify each relationship you establish.

activities.title: Index the subject on social media use by postgraduate students
activities.instructions_md: Index the subject “Use of social media by postgraduate students for academic communication.” Identify at least four concepts, and explain the reasoning behind each choice.

activities.title: Propose index terms for three titles
activities.instructions_md:
For each title below, propose at least four appropriate index terms and briefly justify your choices:
1. “Use of Social Media by University Students for Academic Research in Nigeria.”
2. “Application of Artificial Intelligence in Academic Libraries.”
3. “Preservation of Indigenous Knowledge Resources in Nigerian University Libraries.”

activities.title: Analyse a PRECIS statement
activities.instructions_md: Analyse the statement “Postgraduate students use electronic databases for academic research.” Identify the agent, the action, the object, and the purpose within this statement before applying the exact operator rules prescribed by your own course.

activities.title: Create KWIC and KWOC entries
activities.instructions_md: Create both a KWIC entry and a KWOC entry for the title “Artificial Intelligence Applications in Nigerian University Libraries.”

activities.title: Calculate precision, recall and fallout
activities.instructions_md: A collection contains 800 documents, of which 160 are relevant to a particular search. That search retrieves 100 documents, of which 70 are relevant. Calculate the precision, recall, and fallout for this search.

activities.title: Write indicative and informative abstracts
activities.instructions_md: Write a 60–80 word indicative abstract and a separate 100–150 word informative abstract for a hypothetical paper about information-literacy training and database use among postgraduate students.

activities.title: Prepare a full abstract from a research article
activities.instructions_md:
Working from a research article of approximately 1,500–3,000 words (your own choice, or one supplied by your lecturer):
1. Identify the title.
2. Identify the research problem.
3. Identify the objectives.
4. Identify the methodology.
5. Identify the major findings.
6. Identify the conclusion.
7. Prepare a 150–250 word informative abstract.
8. Identify five appropriate keywords.
